## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymized — JCCP's own submission guidelines confirm a mandatory "masked reviewing system for all submissions" (verified live 2026-07-20 at apa.org/pubs/journals/ccp/submit; "masked" is APA/psychology's field-specific term for double-anonymized review, not a distinct lighter policy) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | *(pending — APA has cross-journal transfer for some titles)* |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | No (per APA default) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | *(pending — typically 1-2 rounds)* |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | *(pending)* |
### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No (follows APA publisher default) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | Conditional / disclosure-based — no editorial pre-approval needed, but disclosure + AI-tool attribution is mandatory in Methods/Acknowledgments (confirmed live 2026-07-20 via APA's publisher-wide generative-AI policy page, apa.org/pubs/journals/resources/publishing-tips/policy-generative-ai) |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 4 — APA's policy permits AI use for idea generation, drafting, analysis, and code as long as disclosed/cited; the only hard limits are no AI authorship and no entry of confidential submitted content into AI tools |
| **Summary** | Follows APA publisher AI policy: authors must disclose use of generative AI tools (ChatGPT, etc.) in manuscript preparation. AI cannot satisfy authorship criteria. APA requires explicit disclosure in the Methods/Acknowledgments section. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/policies/ |

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Medium-High — clinical psychology has internationalizing reach; cross-cultural treatment efficacy studies regularly published |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium — accepts non-Western treatment-adaptation data within RCT framework |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — race, ethnicity, gender, LGBTQ-affirmative therapy papers regularly published |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Clinical psychology — psychotherapy techniques (1,436 articles), child/adolescent psychosocial development (2,290), anxiety/depression psychometrics (672), substance abuse treatment (620), personality disorders / psychopathology (526) per OpenAlex |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **clinical psychology treatment or prevention contribution** — RCT-friendly, outcome-focused, with clear clinical implications. EIC Joanne Davila's editorial line prioritizes treatment + prevention.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Format-noncompliant manuscripts returned without review. Desk rejection broadly in 20–50% range across APA psychology journals.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Dominant — RCT and controlled clinical trials core |
| Qualitative interviews | 1 | Rare; qualitative clinical work typically goes to dedicated qualitative-health venues |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 2 | Occasional; clinical theoretical contributions accepted |
| Mixed methods | 2 | Accepted with quantitative dominance |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed; PRISMA reporting expected |
| Treatment outcome | 5 | Core method |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | 1 — APA-style third-person scholarly register |
| **Expected density** | Almost none |
| **Writing style notes** | APA-style formal academic register; clinical-psychology vocabulary (DSM-5-TR, evidence-based practice, treatment fidelity, effect sizes); CONSORT-style reporting for trials |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from clinical psychology and clinical-health psychology specialists — APA Division 12 (Society of Clinical Psychology) faculty and senior clinicians. Expect deep literacy in CBT, DBT, ACT, IPT, psychodynamic treatments, child/adolescent intervention, substance use treatment, and treatment outcome research methods. Common reviewer demands: "Clinical significance beyond statistical significance?", "Treatment fidelity?", "Long-term follow-up?".

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Clinical psychology + clinical-health psychology specialists | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/ccp |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium — clinical depth high; variance in specialist-population literacy |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) — RCT methodology is the journal's center of gravity |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International clinical-psychology programs; APA Division 12 affiliations |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Format-noncompliant manuscripts returned without review (community evidence: APA editorial practice 2026-05)
- Pure qualitative clinical work (consider Qualitative Health Research, qualitative-psychology venues)
- Manuscripts without treatment / prevention focus
- Failure to disclose AI use per APA publisher policy
- Single-case studies without strong theoretical or clinical-impact justification

### Soft Tax

Low for RCT-tradition clinical authors. Moderate for non-RCT empirical authors — typically requires alignment with treatment-outcome framing. APA format and CONSORT reporting are standard expectations. Long APA review cycle should be planned for.

### Best Suited For

- Randomized controlled treatment trials in clinical psychology
- Child and adolescent psychosocial intervention research
- Psychotherapy outcome and process research
- Anxiety, depression, trauma, substance abuse treatment studies
- Personality disorders and psychopathology research with clinical-impact framing
- Meta-analyses of clinical-treatment literatures
- Digital mental health intervention RCTs

### Not Recommended For

- Pure autoethnography or first-person clinical narratives
- Single-case qualitative analyses (consider qualitative-psychology venues)
- Critical / discursive clinical-psychology papers (consider Theory & Psychology)
- Pure theoretical clinical contributions without empirical test
- Authors needing rapid turnaround

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Clinical Psychology Review](./clinical-psychology-review.md) | If recast as systematic review / meta-analysis; Elsevier; clinical-review specialty |
| 2 | [Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science](./journal-of-psychopathology-and-clinical-science.md) | If the work has psychopathology / mechanism focus; APA family (titled *Journal of Abnormal Psychology* until 2022) |
| 3 | [Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry](./journal-of-child-psychology-and-psychiatry.md) | If the work is child/adolescent focused; ACAMH/Wiley |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top general clinical-psychology venue as "too specialty-focused," JCCP is often a better fit because: it specializes in clinical-treatment outcome research with deep reviewer-pool expertise; RCT-friendly editorial culture; and APA Division 12 affiliation provides built-in clinical audience.
